subject: Optimize toolkit: packaging & quantization guidance for CloudFluent pilot
body:
From: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@cloudfluent.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: m.reed@cloudfluent.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing & quantization — CloudFluent exploratory

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Marcus and I chatted and we think Redwood's Optimize toolkit could materially reduce our inference spend for the recommendation surface. Before we lock a pilot, can you share:

- Typical packaging options for a 3–6 month pilot (credits, capped spend, or commit).
- How discounts are applied when we enable batching/cache vs when we apply quantization (is that a commercial discount or purely engineering guidance?).
- Any constraints or tradeoffs around int8 or int4 quantization for our 70B model (we run a finetuned Llama variant).

We're aiming to run a small production pilot: approx 3M tokens/day, burst to ~20 req/s, 99th pct latency target <= 200ms for the recommend endpoint. Attaching a short SOW outline.

Thanks — can we get a commercial + technical recommendation this week?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lane
Head of ML Platforms, CloudFluent
(attachment: CloudFluent_SOW_v1.pdf)

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@cloudfluent.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing & quantization — CloudFluent exploratory

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. I'm looping in Dylan (SE) and Monica (CS) to provide technical guidance and an initial commercial framework. Quick thoughts up front:

- For a 3–6 month pilot we typically offer a mixed model: a small pilot credit + optional capped trial rate, then a conversion to a short-term commit (monthly) with volume tiers if you want predictability.
- We can tie an operational discount (5–20%) to enabling the Optimize toolkit best practices (batching + KV cache) since those have measurable token reductions. Quantization recommendations are technical but we can propose a commercial concession that phases with acceptability (e.g., 10% discount if you agree to enable int8 on non-latency-critical routes).

Dylan — can you draft the guidance on batching/cache windows and expected token savings for their profile? Monica — can you and I draft the pilot commercial that includes the credit, conversion path, and a proposed discount table?

Happy to jump on a call Thursday if that helps.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@cloudfluent.com>, avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing & quantization — CloudFluent exploratory

Sarah / Avery — quick technical note on sizing / tradeoffs based on the numbers you shared:

Summary recommendations (short):
- Batching: set an adaptive batcher with a 20ms aggregation window for the recommend route. For 20 req/s bursts this should increase GPU utilization and reduce per-token overhead by ~18–25%.
- KV/prefix cache: enable a 12-hour warm KV cache for common user prefixes; expect additional 10–15% token reduction on repeated contexts.
- Quantization: start with int8 (GPTQ/LLM.int8) on the 70B variant for non-real-time scoring paths — we expect ~2x memory reduction and minimal quality loss for recommendations. Avoid int4 on the primary latency-sensitive path until we validate quality.
- Latency: with batching + int8 on a dedicated pool we can keep median latency <<100ms and 95th ~150–200ms provided we reserve a small burst pool for peak traffic.

Notes / risks:
- int8 may need a short eval (1–2k prompt set) to confirm no regressions in ranking/ctr metrics. We can include quality windows in the pilot SLOs.
- Batching brings tail sensitivity: we'll couple batching with our dynamic priority queue so high-priority real-time traffic bypasses multi-request batching.

If useful I can produce a small eval harness (we've used it before) and tie the metric pass/fail to the commercial concession.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing & quantization — CloudFluent exploratory

Thanks Dylan — that line items up with our internal thinking. A couple clarifications:

- Our 3M tokens/day estimate is for the recommend endpoint only. We expect another 0.5M tokens/day for session/context ops.
- We can run an eval set for int8 — what sample size do you recommend? We'll aim for 2k prompts across top-10 classes unless you advise otherwise.
- Commercially: Marcus is pushing for a capped spend pilot (so we don't blow past budget) + an option to convert to a 6-month commit with a discount. What would a 6-month commit need to look like to get 15%–20% off list?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sarah

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@cloudfluent.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing & quantization — CloudFluent exploratory

Sarah / Marcus — thanks for the details. Below is a concise commercial proposal and recommended next steps.

Commercial proposal (pilot -> commit):
- Pilot: $25,000 prepaid credit covering usage up to an equivalent of ~8M tokens (we'll instrument daily spend alerts). If you exceed the cap we throttle and notify — no surprise overages.
- Eval & quality gate: we run int8 evaluation on your 2k prompt set during week 1; if pass (no meaningful CTR drop) Redwood will provide an additional $5k credit and enable int8 in the pilot pool. If fail, we default back to float16 for the pilot route and proceed with batching/KV only.
- Conversion discount: if you convert to a 6-month commit within the pilot period at the committed monthly token volume equal to pilot average * 1.1, we offer a 15% discount off list for the recommend route. A 12-month commit would move to 20%.
- Ops commitments: dedicated small burst pool, SLOs for latency at 95th <=200ms, and weekly call cadence during the pilot.

Next steps:
1) Sign the attached SOW (CloudFluent_SOW_v1.pdf) and return a countersigned copy.
2) We'll provision a pilot tenant and schedule the int8 eval harness (Dylan will own this).
3) Kickoff call — propose Tue 8/17 10am PT.

I've attached the cost model projection we referenced and a draft SOW. Monica and I can tighten the commercial language once you confirm the preferred commit term.

If that all sounds good I'll send a DocuSign link for the SOW.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
